newsitem.title: ISRAEL: Soros helps form Israeli venture capital fund.
newsitem.headline: Soros helps form Israeli venture capital fund.

text.p: Quantum Industrial Holdings Ltd, a fund managed by the Soros group, is forming a venture capital fund with Comverse Technology Inc to invest in Israeli high tech companies, a Comverse executive said on Wednesday.
Yaacov Koren said the two sides would each hold half the $30 million fund to be called ComSor Investment Fund BV, based in the Netherlands.
He said the fund would invest in high technology companies without focusing on specific segments. "We have not limited ourselves to specific areas of high technology," he said.
He said ComSor would consider increasing the size of the fund and perhaps take on additional investors but that there are no immediate plans to do so.
"The current stockholders have the resources to expand the funds for additional investments....The amount is reasonable for now," Koren said.
Quantum Industrial Holdings is a New York-based private equity investment management firm founded by George Soros. Its parent, Quantum Group, has assets of approximately $15 billion.

Comverse, which is based in Woodbury, New York but conducts much of its activities in Israel, develops and manufactures computer and telecommunications systems. Its CTI Capital unit, which Koren heads, invests in Israeli high tech start-up companies and will act as ComSor's Israeli agent.

In the past year Soros companies have taken stakes in Israel's Indigo NV, a manufacturer of computerised print equipment, and El Rov Ltd, a property developer. Soros also participated in an abortive bid for Bank Hapoalim.
